title: Judges, juries and lawyers in civil cases
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:38Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: Neither bank point covers civil cases: both teach criminal jury trials in NSW, with a jury of 12 deciding guilt and no point on judges managing civil cases, a six-person civil jury, or lawyers presenting each side, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Judges, juries and lawyers in civil cases
card: A judge manages the case before and during the hearing. In case management, the judge sets timelines and helps the parties narrow the issues in dispute, so the hearing is shorter and more focused.
A judge also decides questions of law, such as which rules apply and what evidence is allowed. If there is no jury, the judge decides the facts too.

In some civil cases in Victoria, a jury of six people may decide the facts, such as what happened. The judge tells the jury the law to apply. A jury is not used in every civil case, and a party may choose to have one.
Lawyers present each side. They advise their client, prepare the case, question witnesses and argue for their client's position.
draft.remember: The judge manages the case and decides law. A jury of six may decide facts. Lawyers argue for each side.

a.q: In a civil trial with a jury, which task belongs to the jury rather than the judge?
opts: Deciding what happened on the facts
Deciding which rules of law apply
a.why: A civil jury of six may decide the facts, such as what happened. The judge decides questions of law and manages the case. Lawyers, not the jury, question witnesses for each side.

b.q: Before a civil hearing in Geelong, a judge meets both parties and gets them to agree on which issues are still in dispute. What is the main purpose of this step?
opts: To shorten and focus the hearing on the real issues
To let the judge decide the facts without a jury
To allow the lawyers to give evidence themselves
To make the jury responsible for the law in the case
b.why: This is case management. Narrowing the issues means the hearing deals only with what is truly disputed, which saves time. It does not decide who has a jury, and the lawyers present each side rather than give evidence.
b.clue: Which role does the judge play before the hearing?

a.best: Deciding what happened on the facts

b.best: To shorten and focus the hearing on the real issues
